title: REALIZATIONS OF HOMOLOGY CLASSES AND PROJECTION AREAS
abstract: This paper explores the relationship between convex geometry and algebraic geometry, focusing on two interconnected problems regarding projections of geometric objects in four-dimensional spaces.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you have a convex body in 4-dimensional space, and you project it onto a 2-dimensional plane. What can you say about the areas of these projections?

We can think of this problem in terms of mixed volumes, which describe how convex bodies interact with each other.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content: The Plücker relations for the Grassmannian Gr(2, 4) over the triangular hyperfield T2 provide a key to understanding these projections. We can define a set ∆(T2) of tuples of six nonnegative real numbers that satisfy certain conditions.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content: Our results show that the set ∆(T2) is closely related to the set of realizable homology classes in P^4. We can use mixed volumes to construct examples of realizable classes.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: Our work has implications for algebraic geometry and convex geometry. We can use our results to study the projection volumes of convex bodies and the homology classes of algebraic surfaces.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content: Our key innovation is the use of mixed volumes to study the projections of convex bodies. We also introduce a new Lorentzian condition for matrices, which plays a crucial role in our results.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content: You can try to construct your own examples of realizable homology classes using mixed volumes. Can you find a convex body whose projection has a large mixed volume?
